content.title: About
content.content: A whole fried egg served in fast‑food outlets or restaurants is a quickly prepared dish where a whole chicken egg is cooked on a skillet until the desired doneness. It is usually served plain, sometimes with a pinch of salt and pepper.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fried eggs are often listed as a standalone menu item or as part of a breakfast combo.
By 1936 fried eggs were already a staple in American diners.
Cooking styles such as sunny side up, over easy, over medium, and over hard give different yolk textures.
Eggs are one of the most affordable protein sources in fast‑food cuisine.
High‑heat frying creates a crisp edge that locks in moisture.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A large egg provides about 6 g of high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain vitamin B12, riboflavin, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Choline
items.content: Choline in the yolk is important for liver function and brain health.

items.title: Lutein and zeaxanthin
items.content: These carotenoids help maintain eye health and protect against age‑related macular degeneration.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Eggs contain virtually no carbs, making them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Salmonella risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs may harbor Salmonella; it is advisable to cook the yolk through.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: The yolk contains about 186 mg of cholesterol; individuals with elevated cholesterol should moderate intake.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some people are allergic to egg proteins and should avoid the product.

items.title: Cooking oil considerations
items.content: Using excessive oil can add calories and potentially introduce trans fats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried eggs can be served on their own, with toast, in burgers, salads, or as part of a breakfast plate. Optional toppings include salt, pepper, herbs, or sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared fried eggs are best eaten immediately. If needed, store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for no more than 2 hours and reheat thoroughly before consumption.
